round1_to_round2.comment: All five agents adopted the round-1 corrections (NTM EPS ~$9.9-10.05, 1/3 FY28 + 2/3 FY29 window, ~$2.6B net cash with ~85M shares, $1.354B buyback remaining, stale October-hike odds, guide-implied Q4 +14-16%). The EPS fix lifted agents 2 and 5; the cash fix and multiple cuts lowered agents 1 and 4. The mean ladder barely moved (P(>=356) 0.528 to 0.523, every strike within 0.005), while the cross-agent spread fell by about a third (max 0.065 to 0.042). The remaining disagreement is multiple judgment (37-40x P/E, 7-8x EV/sales), not facts.

disagreements.topic: Exit multiples (the only material residual gap)
disagreements.positions: P/E 37x (agent_3), 38x (agent_1), 39x (agent_4), 40x (agents 2 and 5); EV/NTM sales 7.0x (agent_3), 7.5x (agents 1 and 4), 8.0x (agents 2 and 5). Fair values $366-405.
disagreements.resolution: Not settleable by fact-checks. Arguments for the lower end are verified: FY27 SBC $628.9M (~21% of revenue) exceeds non-GAAP net income, the 10Y is ~5.2%, and npm data show relative share loss to Postgres. Arguments for the higher end are also verified: Q2 beat its guide by 5.1%, Atlas ~29% for five quarters, and the H2 raise was 'mainly due to Atlas'. The mean (~38.8x, ~7.7x) is a fair centre; fair value ~$388.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 FY27 8-K Ex.99.1 (SBC, guidance, Atlas and EA growth); npm registry API.

disagreements.topic: How much of the Q2 beat was durable (FY28 growth 19% vs 20% vs 21%)
disagreements.resolution: EA & other grew +13% in Q1 and +36% in Q2, so part of the 5% Q2 beat was lumpy term-license revenue that will not repeat and sets tough comparisons. But the release says the H2 guide raise was mainly due to Atlas. That supports ~19-20% as the centre, and makes the March-2027 FY28 guide the key event rather than a median shift. Effect on value is ~$5-10/share across the range; left at the mean.
disagreements.evidence: Q1 FY27 release ('EA & other revenue up more than 13%'); Q2 FY27 release ('EA & other revenue up approximately 36%'; 'H2 raise mainly due to Atlas').

disagreements.topic: March-print base rate and bear weight
disagreements.positions: Agents 1, 3 and 4 raised bear weight to 27%, agent_5 to 26%, agent_2 held 25%. Agent_5 cites -27% (2025) and -22% (2026) March reactions.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed: -26.9% on Mar 6, 2025 and -22.2% on Mar 3, 2026 (daily closes). Two of the last two March guides produced >20% one-day drops, and the FY27 guide already implies Q4 +14-16%. A 25-27% bear weight is appropriate; the mean ladder already carries it.
disagreements.evidence: Twelve Data daily MDB closes around both prints.

disagreements.positions: agent_4 uses npm, PyPI, DB-Engines and hiring data to move 2 points from bull to bear; agents 2 and 3 treat Postgres/DocumentDB as a multiple cap.
disagreements.resolution: Verified. MongoDB driver downloads rose ~64% y/y, but 'pg' rose ~345%, so relative share of the pair halved (~43% to ~21%). It supports a multiple cap and bear-tail weight, not a cut to the median revenue path (Atlas still ~29%).
disagreements.evidence: api.npmjs.org downloads for 'mongodb' and 'pg', Sep 2025 vs Sep 2026.

disagreements.positions: Agents 1, 3, 4, 5 and the round-1 supervisor describe ~$240-245 as '~5.3-5.5x NTM EV/sales on ~$4.1B'.
disagreements.resolution: Arithmetic slip, shared by the round-1 supervisor. At $240 with ~85M shares and ~$2.4-2.6B cash, EV is ~$18B: ~5.4x today's NTM revenue (~$3.3B) and ~4.4x the Sep-2027 NTM ($4.1B). The price level is still right (it sits in the Mar-Apr 2026 low zone and near the post-March-print closes); only the multiple description changes.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 FY27 balance sheet ($2.41B cash and ST investments, no debt); 85.8M fully diluted shares.

one_month_reasoning: No MDB earnings in the window (Q3 FY27 reports in early December); the CEO exit, Investor Day, buyback top-up and Sep 30 PCE repricing are in the $356 close, and the in-window events (Oct 27-28 FOMC, late-October hyperscaler results, CEO-search headlines) are roughly symmetric, so I keep the round-2 mean (median ~$357).
confidence_reason: Round 2 left no factual disagreement that moves the forecast. My checks (EA lumpiness, npm share shift, March-print drawdowns) confirmed points the agents already priced in. The residual gap is multiple judgment, which evidence cannot settle, so I keep the forecasters' round-2 mean.
thesis_break_reason: About $240 (-33%): ~5.4x today's NTM EV/sales (~$3.3B) or ~4.4x Sep-2027 NTM revenue (~$4.1B), inside the Mar-Apr 2026 low zone ($216-260) and near where the last two March prints landed. Reaching it without a broad market crash would most likely mean a FY28 guide well below ~18% in March 2027 (confirming the guide-implied +14-16% Q4), Atlas sliding toward 20%, or go-to-market departures during the CEO search. Agents range $230-245; the correction is to the multiple description, not the level.
key_drivers: The March 2027 FY28 guide: the FY27 guide implies Q4 +14-16% against a +27% comparison, and the last two March prints fell 27% and 22% in a day.
Beat quality: Q2 beat its guide by 5.1%, but EA & other swung from +13% (Q1) to +36% (Q2); the H2 raise was mainly Atlas, which has held ~29% for five quarters.
Earnings power: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 ~$9.9-10.05 and NTM revenue ~$4.1B on 20% growth and +150bp/yr margins; SBC at ~21% of revenue caps the multiple.
Leadership: interim CEO Ittycheria (part-time risk as a Sequoia partner); naming a permanent CEO is the main re-rating catalyst.
Relative mindshare loss to Postgres (npm 'pg' downloads +345% y/y vs 'mongodb' +64%) is a multiple cap and bear-tail driver; it is not yet visible in Atlas growth.

fair_value.reason: Round-2 inputs are now consistent across agents: NTM EPS ~$9.9-10.05, NTM revenue ~$4.1-4.15B, ~$2.6B net cash, ~85M fully diluted shares. At the mean multiples (~38.8x P/E, ~7.7x EV/sales), P/E gives ~$388 and EV/sales ~$402. Weighting the P/E leg more heavily because SBC is ~21% of revenue, and allowing for March-guide risk, gives ~$388, the round-2 agent mean ($388.6), down from my round-1 $390.

summary: Round 2 converged: every agent adopted the round-1 corrections, the fair-value range narrowed to $366-405 (mean $389), and the cross-agent ladder spread fell by a third while the mean barely moved (P(close >= $356 on 2027-09-30) = 0.523). My checks confirmed the new points the agents raised: Q2's beat was partly lumpy EA revenue, the last two March guides caused one-day drops of 27% and 22%, and npm data show relative share loss to Postgres. What is left is judgment on multiples, so I keep the round-2 mean ladder with low confidence, a ~$388 fair value and a $240 thesis break. The March 2027 FY28 guide, not the CEO search, is the event that decides whether the stock re-rates.
